blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Import and export taxes in practice shape the real economics of a trade deal. A product's final price at destination is rarely the sum of cost and margin alone. It is cost, plus freight, plus insurance, plus import duty, plus local VAT, plus any small additional levies the destination country adds. Miss one of these, and the margin the commercial team thought they had can vanish entirely.

The intermediate discipline is to calculate the landed cost of every product in every destination before it is priced, not after it is sold. Because duty rates change, sometimes quickly, a rate that was correct six months ago may no longer be. And although free trade agreements can reduce duties substantially, they usually require specific documentation — without it, the lower rate is not applied and the company pays the full amount.

Good trade operators keep a live duty table. It is not glamorous work. It is the difference between real margin and imaginary margin.

items.q: According to the text, the final price at destination is made up of…
options: cost, freight, insurance, duty, VAT and any extra levies
items.why: "It is cost, plus freight, plus insurance, plus import duty, plus local VAT, plus any small additional levies."

items.q: When should landed cost be calculated, according to the text?
options: Once a year, at the budget review
items.why: "calculate the landed cost… before it is priced, not after it is sold."

items.q: Why might a duty rate that was correct six months ago be wrong today?
options: Because duty rates change, sometimes quickly
Because the margin was too low
items.why: "Because duty rates change, sometimes quickly, a rate that was correct six months ago may no longer be."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A free trade agreement guarantees a lower rate automatically.
Keeping a live duty table is worth the effort.
Missing one cost can wipe out the expected margin.
Landed cost should be known before pricing.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o acordo reduz o imposto apenas COM a documentação específica — não é automático.

items.q: The phrase "imaginary margin" at the end suggests that…
options: margins should never be discussed with clients
commercial teams invent their numbers on purpose
a margin can look real on paper but disappear once all landed costs are counted
items.why: Inferência: sem calcular o custo posto no destino, a margem existe só no papel — não no resultado real.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver explicando o caso ao novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Come and look at this shipment with me. On paper, this was one of our best deals last quarter — solid volume, a healthy margin, everyone was happy. But when the numbers finally settled, it lost money. Quietly. Nobody noticed for weeks.

Here is what happened. The destination country raised its import duty by three points, and nobody updated our pricing model. So we quoted the client using the old rate, we won the business, and then customs charged us the new one. That gap came straight out of our margin.

And it gets worse. There was a free trade agreement that could have cut the duty almost in half — but only with the right certificate of origin. We never sent it, so the lower rate simply did not apply. We paid the full amount.

The lesson is not complicated. Before you price anything, you calculate the landed cost — freight, insurance, duty, VAT, every little levy — for that exact destination, on that exact day. And you keep the duty table live, because these rates change without telling you. Real margin or imaginary margin: this is where the difference is decided.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did last quarter's 'best deal' actually lose money?
options: The client refused to pay the invoice
The destination raised import duty and the pricing model was not updated
Freight costs doubled after the quote
items.why: "The destination country raised its import duty… and nobody updated our pricing model."

items.q: What happened with the free trade agreement in this case?
options: It could have cut the duty, but the certificate of origin was never sent
It applied automatically and saved the deal
It did not exist for that route
It was cancelled by the destination country
items.why: "only with the right certificate of origin. We never sent it, so the lower rate simply did not apply."

items.q: What does Oliver tell the analyst to do BEFORE pricing anything?
options: Wait for customs to confirm the invoice
Ask the client for the current duty rate
Add a fixed 10% buffer to every quote
Calculate the landed cost for that exact destination and day
items.why: "Before you price anything, you calculate the landed cost… for that exact destination, on that exact day."

items.q: When Oliver says the deal lost money "quietly", he implies that…
options: the loss was small and unimportant
the problem went unnoticed until it was too late to fix the quote
the finance team hid the numbers on purpose
items.why: Inferência: "Nobody noticed for weeks" — o prejuízo passou despercebido, não era visível de imediato.

items.q: What is the main point Oliver wants the analyst to take away?
options: Free trade agreements should always be avoided
Duty rates rarely change, so old tables are fine
Pricing should be left to the customs broker
Live, destination-specific landed cost is what protects real margin
items.why: Inferência: ele fecha com custo posto, tabela atualizada e a distinção entre margem real e imaginária.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We only price after we know the landed cost." Landed cost is…
options: the freight bill on its own
the total cost of the goods delivered to the destination, with all charges included
the profit margin on the deal
items.why: Landed cost = custo posto no destino: mercadoria mais todos os encargos até chegar ao comprador.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The lower rate under the deal only applies if you send the ___."
items.why: Specific documentation = documentação específica; sem ela, a alíquota menor não é concedida.

items.q: "The destination added a small extra levy on top of the duty." A levy is…
options: a charge or tax imposed by an authority
items.why: Levy = taxa imposta por uma autoridade, cobrada além do imposto principal.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When we forgot the duty, the whole margin seemed to ___ overnight."
items.why: To vanish = desaparecer; a margem some quando um custo é esquecido.

items.q: "We update our live table every week." A live table is…
options: a printed archive from last year
a table of rates kept current and updated as things change
items.why: Live table = tabela atualizada, mantida sempre com os valores vigentes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em operações de comércio exterior. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the new landed-cost model." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the live duty table to every desk next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The margin thought to be safe was wiped out by the new duty." It was…
items.why: Wiped out = zerado, completamente eliminado.

items.q: "Nobody followed through on updating the duty table." They…
options: failed to carry the task to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — o que não aconteceu aqui.

items.q: "We need to factor in insurance and every small levy before we quote." To factor in means to…
items.why: Factor in = incluir no cálculo, considerar no total.
